title: runtime: add KV cache fragmentation metrics + structured logging
author: Caleb Johnson
description:
Motivation: We’ve been chasing bursty p95/p99 spikes that correlate with KV cache fragmentation + allocation churn. Today we don’t have stable, low-cardinality metrics to (a) quantify fragmentation per pool/region/model family, (b) alert on allocator failure pressure, and (c) attribute individual request latency spikes to allocator/eviction/compaction events. This PR adds a first pass of runtime metrics + structured logs to support ENG-2842 (instrumentation baseline) and feed the upcoming compaction work.

What’s in this PR: Adds KV cache fragmentation metrics with consistent naming, units, and tag set; adds structured logging events to correlate allocator state with tail latency (and to make incident triage less guessy); adds unit tests to lock down metric names/tags and prevent accidental high-cardinality additions.

Metrics added (names/units): 1) redwood_runtime_kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio (gauge, unit=ratio 0..1). Definition: 1 - (largest_free_contiguous_bytes / total_free_bytes). Note: this is allocator-local (per device) and intended to capture “holes” / non-coalesced free space rather than overall utilization. 2) redwood_runtime_kv_cache_free_bytes (gauge, unit=bytes). 3) redwood_runtime_kv_cache_total_bytes (gauge, unit=bytes). 4) redwood_runtime_kv_cache_alloc_failures_total (counter, unit=count). Increments on allocator failure that would otherwise force eviction/admission-control fallback. 5) redwood_runtime_kv_cache_evictions_total (counter, unit=count). This is a shallow counter (eviction initiated), not eviction success/failure. 6) redwood_runtime_kv_cache_search_ns (histogram, unit=nanoseconds). Tracks allocator free-list search/placement overhead (fast path regression guard).

Tags/labels (low cardinality by design): region, pool, model_family, runtime_build, device (coarse ID like gpu0/gpu1). Deliberately NOT tagging by tenant_id, request_id, model_id, or context_length to avoid cardinality blowups. For model_family we use the existing runtime model taxonomy (e.g., llama, mistral, qwen) rather than specific version strings.

Structured logs: Adds JSON structured events emitted at INFO with sampling (default 1/512 requests; configurable) and always-on WARN events on allocator failure. Events: kv_cache_fragmentation_snapshot (periodic / sampled, includes fragmentation_ratio, free_bytes, total_bytes, active_sequences, evictions_last_10s, search_ns_p50/p95), kv_cache_alloc_failure (on failure, includes requested_bytes, free_bytes, fragmentation_ratio, admission_control_state), kv_cache_eviction (sampled, includes victim_count and reason). Logs include region/pool/model_family and trace_id when available so SRE can pivot from a p99 trace to allocator context.

Config/flags: Adds runtime config keys (default safe/off-ish): runtime.observability.kv_cache_metrics_enabled=true (metrics are cheap and always-on), runtime.observability.kv_cache_structured_logs_enabled=false, runtime.observability.kv_cache_structured_logs_sample_rate=0.001953125 (1/512), runtime.observability.kv_cache_failure_logs_enabled=true.

Testing: Unit tests validate: exact metric names and types; allowed tag set (fails if a new tag is added without updating allowlist); model_family derivation stable for common models; structured log payload schema includes required fields and does not accidentally include request prompts or other sensitive payload. Also adds a small allocator-mock test that exercises fragmentation_ratio definition edge cases (no free space, fully free, multiple free segments).

Rollout notes: This is observability-only and should be safe to land. Metrics are behind the central telemetry schema already; the runtime exporter uses the existing allowlisted metric registry. Structured logs remain disabled by default and can be enabled per region/pool during the compaction canary (ENG-2851) to reduce noise.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): 1) dashboards/alerts in observability-pack (tracked separately) 2) compaction metrics (bytes moved, compaction time, compaction budget exceeded) will come with the compaction engine PR 3) possibly revise fragmentation definition once allocator refactor lands (block map).

Notes for SRE: The intended initial alert signals are alloc_failures_total rate > 0 sustained + fragmentation_ratio > 0.65 in the same pool, correlated with p99. This PR just provides the raw ingredients; thresholds will be tuned during canary.

Refs: Linear ENG-2842, ENG-2841; internal support INT-1183; support context SUP-4410; postmortem PM-2025-02-11 (allocator failures during bursts).
commits: runtime/metrics: add kv cache fragmentation + allocator failure counters
runtime/logging: emit structured kv cache events (sampled) and failure warnings
runtime/config: add knobs for kv cache structured logs + sampling
tests: lock down metric names/tags and log schema
docs(in-code): add comments on fragmentation definition + cardinality guardrails
review_conversation: Omar El-Sayed: Fragmentation ratio definition looks good, but can you clarify in-code that it’s measuring contiguity (coalescing) and not utilization? That’s an easy confusion during incidents.
Caleb Johnson (author): Good call. Added comment above the gauge and in kv_cache_metrics.h with the exact definition and a small example (two free segments => high frag even if lots of free bytes).

Allison Grant: Please avoid any tag that could drift into high cardinality. model_family is okay but make sure it can’t fall back to model_id. Also, do we have a test preventing adding tenant/request IDs?

Caleb Johnson (author): Updated model_family derivation to hard-fail to "unknown" if taxonomy doesn’t recognize the model (no fallback to model_id). Added allowlisted tag tests; adding a new tag now breaks tests unless explicitly approved.

Rafael Mendes: For kv_cache_alloc_failure logs, can we include admission control state and a stable error code? During burst incidents we need to know if this triggered backpressure vs eviction vs outright 5xx.

Caleb Johnson (author): Added fields: admission_control_state (open|throttled|closed), action_taken (evict|backpressure|reject), and error_code=KV_ALLOC_FAIL. Also ensured we do not include request payloads.
Marcus Reed: Any measurable overhead from the histogram (search_ns) in the allocator fast path? We’ve been sensitive to anything on decode.

Caleb Johnson (author): search_ns uses a cheap monotonic clock sampling 1/128 allocations by default; on hot path it’s a branch + two reads. Added a microbenchmark assertion in tests (guarded) and a note to revisit once block map lands.
Samir Qureshi: Nit: rename "device" label to "gpu" to match other runtime metrics? Otherwise dashboards end up inconsistent.
Caleb Johnson (author): Switched label key to gpu and updated existing label map helper to keep everything consistent. Tests updated accordingly.
Omar El-Sayed: Approved once the last label rename lands.
Allison Grant: Approved. Thanks for the cardinality guardrails.
Rafael Mendes: Approved; please ping SRE when you want to enable structured logs in a canary region so we can watch volume.
release_notes: Runtime now exports KV cache fragmentation + allocator pressure metrics (by region/pool/model_family) and supports optional sampled structured logs for KV cache allocator events. No behavior change; structured logs remain disabled by default.
